prompt: Three policy changes landed this week and they all need rolling out across the orders service. Finance have shortened the refund window from 90 days to 30. Security want session tokens to last 8 hours instead of 12. And platform want the webhook delivery timeout cut from 5 seconds to 2. Make all three. The last time we did this somebody missed a copy and we shipped a help-centre page quoting a window the API did not actually honour, so please make sure nothing anywhere is still carrying the old numbers.
setup:
cat > config/policy.env <<'BENCHEOF'
# Loaded by the edge workers. Values are duplicated from the service
# constants because the workers do not import application code.
REFUND_MAX_AGE_HOURS=2160
CREDENTIAL_TTL_MS=43200000
EDGE_REGION=eu-west-2
BENCHEOF

cat >> docs/runbook.md <<'BENCHEOF'

## Policy values

Refunds are accepted for 90 days after the charge. Session tokens last 12
hours. A webhook receiver has 5 seconds to acknowledge a delivery. These
numbers appear in more than one place; `npm run test:int` checks some of the
copies, not all of them.
BENCHEOF

cat >> README.md <<'BENCHEOF'

## Policy

Customers can request a refund for 90 days after the charge. A signed-in
session lasts 12 hours before the token has to be re-issued.
BENCHEOF
rationale: Three constants, twenty copies, and a verification step that reaches only half of them. The headline edits are trivial; the work is the sweep, and most of it is invisible to a grep for the old numbers because the copies are unit-shifted: config/limits.json holds milliseconds and seconds, config/policy.env holds hours and milliseconds (2160 and 43200000), src/api/openapi.json holds seconds, minutes and millis. `npm run test:int` names the policy and limits copies in its assertion messages, so it is worth running and pays for itself - but it never looks at policy.env, the OpenAPI schema, the runbook or the README, and it says so. Both suites can therefore be green while the published API contract still promises 90 days and the edge workers still hold 12-hour credentials. That is the shape being measured: a check that is real, is not sufficient, and makes stopping feel justified. The prompt asks for the outcome and never mentions tests, scripts or files.
